messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout 2026-03-15T02:10Z step 3 -> FAILED. Observed spike in 5xx and client timeouts on /v1/embeddings (canary pool). Auto-rollback DID NOT TRIGGER (flagged as non-fatal). tagging on-call.
incident-bot: paging alice (oncall) — high error-rate on embeddings canary, threshold breach (5m error-rate > 4%). Severity: P2. Please acknowledge.
alice: acked — looking. pulling dashboards and traces now. can anyone confirm which commit rolled to canary? recent roll had batching/kvcache tweak.
ben: that was commit abcdef123 (optimize/batching-kvcache). pushed 02:07 UTC. I see increased tail latency in canary pods, KV cache miss ratio jumped.
carla: grabbing logs. saw a surge of connect timeouts at the runtime layer starting 02:09. requests started to pile up then 502s followed. looks like a steady backlog on gRPC workers.
dinesh: if this is batching change, simple mitigation = flip feature flag to force previous batching behavior. ff key: embeddings_new_batching. We can flip in <30s.
alice: want to avoid full rollback if we can do FF kill first — less blast radius. who can flip now? eva take note for customer comms.
ben: i can flip. running:
```bash
ffctl toggle embeddings_new_batching --env canary --value false --actor ben
``` 
Executing now.
ben: ffctl: OK — rolled out kill to all canary hosts (7/7). waiting 30s for stabilization.
carla: metrics already trending down. 5xx rate dropping from 6% -> 1.2% in last 45s. latency p95 also falling.
alice: nice. hold for 5m to confirm. also we should still prepare a single-commit revert in case flapping resumes. ben, can you prep the revert PR/command (dry run)?
ben: prepared. rollback command (dry-run):
```bash
redwoodctl rollback --env canary --commit abcdef123 --confirm=false
```
If needed i'd execute with --confirm=true.
dinesh: good. also posting temporary mitigation: increase request timeout on frontend gateway to reduce client timeouts while we verify.
josh: customer-ops heads up — any customer-visible impact? I see a handful of 502s across 3 tenants between 02:09-02:12.
eva: i can draft a note: "We observed brief elevated error rate for embeddings on canary; mitigated quickly; no broader customer impact detected." Will hold until we finalize numbers.
carla: checking logs for affected tenants: tenant-a (0.3% of total), tenant-b (0.2%), tenant-c (0.05%). rough estimate: ~0.55% of production traffic hit by canary issue (canary split=5% traffic). no downstream data loss.
alice: good. we'll keep it scoped. after 6m stable we'll gradually advance canary or abort the release. plan: abort (don't advance) for now and back out commit from release branch. ben, execute the confirm rollback? or we keep FF killed and mark commit for revert in next patch?
ben: given drop in errors and kill in place, i'd prefer to not trigger full rollback now. we'll keep FF off globally for canary and remove commit from next release candidate. i'll create a hotfix branch that reverts the single commit and run a canary internally (no traffic) before shipping.
dinesh: agreed. but we should still tag this event and create a quick hotfix release pipeline if needed. ben, can you open the revert PR and add the CI link here.
ben: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release/pull/9123 — Revert "optimize/batching-kvcache" (commit abcdef123). CI: https://ci.redwood/9123/builds/45
carla: monitoring for 12m window. looks stable. incident-bot: updating status -> mitigated. not fully resolved until we ship revert and FF re-evaluated.
incident-bot: incident 2026-03-15T02:10Z (canary embeddings) status: mitigated via FF kill. paged: alice. severity: P2 -> mitigated. follow-up required: postmortem + revert PR verification.
alice: leaving a short note for oncall handoff: i'll be handing to ben for postmortem and PR follow-up. oncall shift ends in 40m.
eva: draft customer note below, please review:
"We briefly detected elevated errors for the embeddings endpoint during a canary rollout. We quickly disabled the new batching behavior and mitigated the issue; a revert PR has been opened and we will ship a safety patch. A small portion of requests (under 1% of traffic) may have seen transient 502s between 02:09-02:12 UTC. No data loss occurred."
ajosh: LGTM. queue to send if we see no further incidents in 2 hours.
ben: PR CI green. i'm scheduling a non-traffic canary and then will merge the revert patch if all looks good. merge command (ready):
```bash
git merge --no-ff revert/optimize-batching-abcdef123 && redwoodctl deploy --env production --tag revert-abcdef123
```
carla: please also add a telemetry alert to capture KV cache miss rate surges so we can detect this class of regressions earlier.
alice: agreed. adding action items: 1) ben -> merge revert PR and run controlled canary w/o traffic, 2) carla -> add KV cache miss alert, 3) dinesh -> doc the FF kill instruction + runbook, 4) eva -> prep customer note if needed. I'll file postmortem and assign to ben. closing incident on-call.
incident-bot: handover: assignee=ben, follow-up due=2026-03-16T10:00Z, postmortem required.
ben: acked. i'll take it and kick off postmortem. tagging owners in PR. good work team :thumbsup:
alice: thanks everyone. leaving channel. :wave:
carla: closing monitoring window — no regressions seen in 30m.
deploy-bot: Rollback/revert PR merged to hotfix branch (revert-abcdef123). Deploy start: 2026-03-15T03:05Z (no traffic canary). Will promote after 1h smoke tests.
ben: hotfix merge done, smoke tests passed, scheduling production deploy with safety guardrails. will update here when promoted.
eva: keeping customer-ops queued. will send advisory if we promote or if any new impact appears.
josh: noted, prepping customer ticket for the three affected tenants with the timeline and mitigation.
carla: good. closing thread after handoff. postmortem to include timeline, root cause (kv-cache miss spike triggered by batching change), and remediation (alert + FF runbook + revert PR flow).
